'''Maxine Fassberg''' ({{langx|he|מקסין פסברג}}; born c. 1953)<ref name=globes>{{cite web |url= http://www.globes.co.il/news/docview.aspx?did=1001106763|title= הפטנט הניהולי של מנכ"לית אינטל ישראל מקסין פסברג|language=Hebrew|trans-title=The Administrative Patent of Intel Israel CEO Maxine Fassberg|first=Nurit|last=Daberet|date=3 March 2016|accessdate=15 January 2017|work=[[Globes (newspaper)|Globes]]}}</ref> is a South African-Israeli retired educator, engineer, and [[Chief executive officer|CEO]]. She [[Aliyah|immigrated]] from South Africa to Israel in 1975 and earned bachelor's and master's degrees in [[chemistry]] at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]. After teaching high school chemistry for a few years, she switched careers and began working for [[Intel]] as a lithography engineer in 1983. She spent the next 33 years in key positions in that company, including factory manager, plant manager, and general manager (CEO) of Intel Israel. She retired in December 2016. She was inducted into the [[List of Women in Technology International Hall of Fame inductees|Women in Technology International Hall of Fame]] in 2009 and was named one of the "10 most powerful women in tech" by [[CNN]] in 2010.

==Early life and education==
Born in [[Johannesburg]] to Ashkenazi Jewish parents from Europe that migrated to South Africa, Fassberg initially [[Aliyah|immigrated]] to Israel with her family in the 1960s and lived in the country for about seven years before they returned to South Africa.<ref name=globes/> Although she studied in an [[ulpan]] in [[Petah Tikva]], she found it difficult to acclimate to Israeli society.<ref name=globes/> She completed high school in South Africa and, in 1975, immigrated to Israel once again.<ref name=ronit/><ref name=ynet>{{cite web |url=https://www.ynetnews.com/articles/0,7340,L-4700655,00.html|title='Think very hard if you really want to marry him'|first1=Sagi|last1=Cohen|first2=Navit|last2=Zomner|date=15 September 2015|accessdate=13 January 2017|work=[[Ynetnews]]}}</ref> She pursued higher education at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], earning her B.Sc. in [[physics]] and [[applied chemistry]] in 1977, her [[diploma of education]] in 1978, and her M.Sc. in [[organic chemistry]] in 1979.<ref name=wizo>{{cite web |url=http://www.wizo.org/program/guest-speakers/10-maxine-fassberg.html|title=Maxine Fassberg|publisher=[[Women's International Zionist Organization]]|accessdate=12 January 2017}}</ref>

==Career==
===Teaching===
After earning her bachelor's degree, Fassberg began teaching high school chemistry at [[ORT Israel]] and [[Alliance Française]] high schools in Jerusalem.<ref name=wizo/> She also trained chemistry teachers at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.<ref name=witi>{{cite web |url=https://www.witi.com/center/witimuseum/halloffame/247708/Maxine-Fassberg-Vice-President,-Technology-and-Manufacturing-Group,-Fab-28-Plant-Manager-General-Manager,-Intel-Israel/|title=Featured Profile: Maxine Fassberg|year=2017|accessdate=12 January 2017|publisher=[[Women in Technology International]] Hall of Fame}}</ref> When her application for a school principal position was rejected, she decided to switch career tracks.<ref name=ynet/><ref name=haaretz>{{cite web |url=https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/business/maxine-fassberg-ceo-of-intel-israel-intel-inside-the-periphery-1.382580|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306011154/http://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/business/maxine-fassberg-ceo-of-intel-israel-intel-inside-the-periphery-1.382580|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 6, 2016|title=Maxine Fassberg, CEO of Intel Israel: Intel, Inside the Periphery|first=Tali|last=Heruti-Sover|date=5 September 2011|accessdate=13 January 2017|work=[[Haaretz]]}}</ref>

===Intel===
[[File:Intel factory, Kiryat Gat industry zone.jpg|right|thumb|[[Intel]] [[Semiconductor fabrication plant|fabrication plant]] in [[Kiryat Gat]], c. 2008]]
{{Quote box
 |width=225px
 |align=right
 |quoted=true
 |bgcolor= 
 |salign=right
 |quote=When I managed the plant in [[Kiryat Gat]], everyone thought I was the secretary.
 |source=–Maxine Fassberg, speaking on the stereotyping of women in management<ref name=marker>{{cite web |url=https://www.themarker.com/tv/1.2261048|title='כשניהלתי את המפעל בקריית גת, כולם חשבו שאני המזכירה'|language=Hebrew|trans-title='When I managed the plant in Kiryat Gat, everyone thought I was the secretary'|first=Hila|last=Weissberg|date=5 March 2014|accessdate=14 January 2017|work=TheMarker}}</ref>
}}
In 1982 Intel launched a recruitment drive to staff its new [[Semiconductor fabrication plant|Fab]]8 plant – its first factory built outside the United States.<ref name=ronit/> Fassberg applied and was hired in 1983 to work as a lithography engineer at Fab8.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.intel.co.il/content/www/il/he/company-overview/bios/maxine-fassberg.html|title=מקסין פסברג|language=Hebrew|trans-title=Maxine Fassberg|publisher=[[Intel]]|accessdate=13 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170116163102/http://www.intel.co.il/content/www/il/he/company-overview/bios/maxine-fassberg.html|archive-date=2017-01-16|url-status=dead}}</ref> After completing a one-year factory training program in [[Arizona]], she returned to Israel to work as a Manufacturing Area Engineer from 1986 to 1987 and a Fab8 Group Leader from 1988 to 1990 and 1992 to 1993.<ref name=boi/> She was a [[polyimide]] engineer in the Portland Technology Development division from 1991 to 1992.<ref name=boi/>

In 1995 Fassberg became part of the start-up team for the company's Fab18 factory in [[Kiryat Gat]], first as public relations manager and then as manager of the engineering division.<ref name=bio/><ref name=boi/> She oversaw the startup of the 45&nbsp;nm chip plant, and subsequent upgrading of the plant to produce 28&nbsp;nm and 22&nbsp;nm chips.<ref name=times/> She was promoted to Fab18 factory manager in 2000, a position she co-held with Alex Kornhauser until 2004, when she was named Fab18 plant manager.<ref name=boi/>

She was appointed vice president of Intel's worldwide technology and marketing group in 2004.<ref name=haaretz/> In January 2006 she was appointed manager of the company's second factory in Israel, Fab28, also in Kiryat Gat.<ref name=wizo/><ref name=witi/> In June 2007 she was named general manager (CEO) of Intel Israel, with responsibility for developing the Intel Israel Site and the Fab28 factory.<ref name=witi/><ref name=haaretz/><ref name=bio/> Under her leadership, exports increased from $1.54 billion in 2007 to $2.7 billion in 2010.<ref name=haaretz/> In 2011 she was overseeing 7,300 employees.<ref name=haaretz/>

Intel credited Fassberg's leadership for creating thousands of new jobs.<ref name=times/> She also encouraged women, [[Arabs]], [[Druze]], and [[Haredi Judaism|Haredi Jews]] to enter the high-tech sector.<ref name=times/> By 2016, approximately 40% of the management positions at the Kiryat Gat plant were held by women, compared to 33% at other Intel factories in Israel.<ref name=globes/> Fassberg herself often experienced prejudice and stereotyping as a woman in senior management. When she co-managed the Fab18 factory with Kornhauser, she says, people thought she was Kornhauser's secretary. Even when she was CEO, men addressed correspondence to her as [[Maxim (given name)|Maxim]], not Maxine.<ref name=globes/><ref name=marker/>

==Memberships==
Fassberg is a member of the Supervisory Council and Audit Committee of the [[Bank of Israel]],<ref name=boi>{{cite web |url=http://www.boi.org.il/en/AboutTheBank/OfficeHolders/Pages/MaxineFassberg.aspx|title=Mrs. Maxine Fassberg|publisher=[[Bank of Israel]]|year=2014|accessdate=13 January 2017}}</ref> the board of directors of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem,<ref name=bio/> and the board of the [[Bloomfield Science Museum]].<ref name=wizo/> She was a member of the Prime Minister's Round Table from 2008 to 2011 and the Advisory Committee to the National Economic Council in the Prime Minister's Office from 2009 to 2011.<ref name=boi/>

==Awards and honors==
Fassberg received the Industry Award of the [[Manufacturers Association of Israel]] in 2011, and the Hugo Ramniceanu Prize in Economics in 2012. She also received two Intel Achievement Awards for her contribution to the "inter-die electric material problem resolution".<ref name=wizo/>

She was inducted into the [[List of Women in Technology International Hall of Fame inductees|Women in Technology International Hall of Fame]] in 2009. In April 2012, [[CNN]] named her one of the "10 most powerful women in tech". In 2014 she was honored as one of the 14 women torch-lighters at the official [[Yom HaAtzmaut|Israel Independence Day]] ceremony.<ref name=wizo/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.jpost.com/National-News/Maxine-351376|title=Meet the Women Lighting the Independence Day Torches: Intel CEO Maxine Fassberg|first=Tamara|last=Zieve|date=5 May 2014|accessdate=12 January 2017|work=[[The Jerusalem Post]]}}</ref>

Fassberg received an honorary doctorate from [[Ben-Gurion University]] in 2013.<ref name=wizo/>

==Personal life==
She is married to Joseph Fassberg, a physician, with whom she has two children.<ref name=witi/> The couple resides in [[Har Adar]].<ref name=ronit>{{cite web |url=https://www.themarker.com/technation/1.504167|title= טובה הכי (2008)|language=Hebrew|trans-title=The Best (2008)|first1=Ronit|last1=Harel|first2=Guy|last2=Grimland|date=5 May 2008|accessdate=14 January 2017|work=[[TheMarker]]}}</ref>
